Excellent
ĕx´cel-lent
adj. (surpassing, of great worth; rendering Hebrew addir, yaqar, Greek diaphoros, kreitton)
From Latin excellens, rising above, towering. In the Authorized Version the word belongs first to God, and only derivatively to anything else.

Biblical Definition

Excellent is chiefly a word about God in Scripture, and its most familiar use is a psalm that begins and ends with it: “O LORD our Lord, how excellent is thy name in all the earth!” (Psa 8:1, 9). The excellency belongs to the Name, to the lovingkindness (Psa 36:7), and to the greatness for which He is praised (Psa 150:2) — and where the word is applied to creatures it is applied to those in whom God has put something of Himself: “the saints that are in the earth, and… the excellent, in whom is all my delight” (Psa 16:3). David's delight rests where God's does. Hebrews takes the comparative and makes it the engine of the whole epistle — a more excellent name than the angels (Heb 1:4), a more excellent sacrifice than Cain's (Heb 11:4) — teaching Christian excellence not as achievement but as comparison: what is better, and why. Psalm 141:5 gives the most bracing use of all, calling a righteous man's rebuke “an excellent oil, which shall not break my head.”

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines excellent as being of great virtue or worth, eminent or distinguished for what is amiable or valuable — and notes that applied to God it denotes perfection above all comparison.

expand to see more

EX´CELLENT, a. Being of great virtue or worth; eminent or distinguished for what is amiable, valuable or laudable.

2. Being of great value or use, applied to things; remarkable for good properties.

3. Distinguished for superior attainments; as an excellent artist.

4. Consummate; complete; in an ill sense.

Key Scripture

Psa 8:1 — "To the chief Musician upon Gittith, A Psalm of David. O LORD our Lord, how excellent is thy name in all the earth! who hast set thy glory above the heavens."

Psa 16:3 — "But to the saints that are in the earth, and to the excellent, in whom is all my delight."

Psa 141:5 — "Let the righteous smite me; it shall be a kindness: and let him reprove me; it shall be an excellent oil, which shall not break my head: for yet my prayer also shall be in their calamities."

Heb 11:4 — "By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh."

Modern Corruption

Excellence detached from its Source and turned into a performance metric — the church borrowing the language of production values while Scripture reserves the word for God and for what He has made better.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The live danger is not that the world has redefined excellence but that the church has imported a merely professional version of it. Where excellence names production values, platform quality, and organizational polish, a congregation can be excellent by every measure it tracks and never once display the thing Psalm 8 means. The principle to recover is that excellence in Scripture is first a divine attribute and only then a derived one.

Psalm 141:5 supplies the corrective that no performance culture can absorb: the righteous man's rebuke is excellent oil. A community serious about excellence in the biblical sense will therefore prize correction above applause, and will measure itself by Hebrews' comparative — is this better, and better by what standard? Abel's sacrifice was more excellent than Cain's not because it was better executed but because it was offered in faith.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew addir (H117), majestic, mighty — the excellent Name of Psalm 8; yaqar (H3368), precious; Greek diaphoros (G1313), differing, hence superior; kreitton (G2909), better — the key word of Hebrews.

expand to see more

Hebrew addir (H117) — majestic, glorious, mighty; how excellent is thy name (Psa 8:1), and the excellent ones of Psa 16:3.

Hebrew tob (H2896) with comparative force — the psalmist's excellent oil of a righteous rebuke (Psa 141:5).

Greek kreitton (G2909) — better, more excellent; the structural word of Hebrews, comparing Christ to every shadow that preceded Him (Heb 1:4).

Usage

"“How excellent is thy name in all the earth!” — the word belongs first to God."

"“The excellent, in whom is all my delight” — David's delight rests where God's does."

"“Let him reprove me; it shall be an excellent oil” — correction prized above applause."
